recent_posts.title: New hope for better accessibility of 3D experiences on the web – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: Canvas-based 3D web experiences are often inaccessible because developers skip semantic fallback content. While the HTML canvas spec has always required fallback content, it's rarely implemented. The emerging HTML-in-canvas proposal (WICG) promises to automatically synchronize visual canvas rendering with semantic HTML, eliminating the costly manual effort of keeping visuals and accessibility fallbacks in sync. Currently available behind a Chrome/Brave feature flag (`chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element`), it lets developers use semantic elements like buttons and render them visually in canvas, ensuring accessibility is built-in rather than bolted on. The post also advocates for planning accessibility from the ideation phase rather than retrofitting it later.

recent_posts.title: WebMCP and the future of the agentic web: do not leave accessibility behind – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: WebMCP is a proposed browser-native standard that lets AI agents interact directly with web pages via predefined tools, removing the guesswork current AI automation relies on. While it promises efficiency gains — like context-aware filtering on e-commerce sites — it must not become a substitute for accessible web design. All parts of the loop (the webpage, the AI agent interface, and the WebMCP layer) must be accessible so users can take manual control at any time. The post warns against treating WebMCP as a 'conforming alternate version' that lets underlying pages remain inaccessible, and calls for disability advocates and accessibility specialists to be included in the standardization process. Practical barriers to testing the proposal — inaccessible demos and costly AI API tiers — are also flagged as issues that could exclude the very users whose feedback matters most.

recent_posts.title: The best shift-left is to shift accessibility into AI model training and not bolting it on later – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: AI models are trained on the web's inaccessible content, inheriting its biases and bad practices. Rather than patching accessibility through prompting, RAG, or MCP workarounds, the argument is that model trainers must integrate accessibility from the ground up — with accessibility specialists and people with disabilities involved in training. Benchmarks like AIMAC show better accessibility results are achievable but currently only with expensive models, which itself contradicts accessibility as a human right. Stronger regulation (e.g., EU AI Act) and louder advocacy are needed to ensure accessibility is baked into AI model training rather than bolted on afterward.

recent_posts.title: Please do not use auto-scrolling content on the web and in applications – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: Auto-scrolling content creates serious accessibility problems, particularly for Android TalkBack screen reader users who experience constant, annoying audio cues (earcons) that make apps nearly unusable. The issue affects both native mobile apps and web pages on Android, though iOS VoiceOver is unaffected. Beyond screen reader users, auto-scrolling harms people with cognitive disabilities, those who get distracted easily, users who rely on zoom, and those with sensory sensitivities. The recommended solution is to eliminate auto-scrolling entirely or provide manual pause/stop controls, as even WCAG-compliant implementations still create poor user experiences.

recent_posts.title: 2026 deserves proactive accessibility governance – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: Cross-platform mobile frameworks like React Native and Flutter have systemic accessibility issues that prevent developers from creating accessible apps, even when they try. While the European Accessibility Act has raised awareness in 2025, major platforms need proactive accessibility governance to prevent regressions and fix long-standing bugs. Native mobile apps tend to be more accessible than cross-platform ones, and developers should check open accessibility issues before choosing a framework. Platforms must provide accessible defaults to enable developers to build accessible products.

recent_posts.title: AI models struggle with accessibility despite automatic testing benchmarks
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft's A11y LLM Eval project benchmarks AI models on accessibility by testing generated code with automatic tools. Results show color contrast failures remain most common, likely because AI learns from existing poor code rather than calculating ratios. The benchmark reveals automatic testing has limited capability and only checks static code patterns. Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools can help AI generate better accessible code by checking contrast ratios before delivery. However, passing automatic tests doesn't guarantee actual accessibility or usability—human knowledge remains essential throughout design, development, content creation, and testing stages.

recent_posts.title: Better accessibility context for your artificial intelligence agents – help them help you – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables AI coding assistants to access real accessibility tree data from browsers, reducing hallucinations when generating accessible code. Chrome DevTools MCP server provides snapshots of page semantics and accessibility information that AI agents can use as context. This approach helps shift accessibility testing left by giving developers and AI tools actual semantic data rather than relying on assumptions, though human verification with assistive technologies remains essential.

recent_posts.title: Five years after EU accessibility directive shows slow progress and weak enforcement
recent_posts.summary: Five years after the EU Web Accessibility Directive deadline, compliance remains elusive for most public sector websites. Despite some progress, enforcement is weak, accessibility overlays are misused as shortcuts, and basic requirements like keyboard support are still neglected. The directive has strengthened the European Accessibility Act and influenced accessibility statements, but systematic progress is too slow. Universities only recently began integrating accessibility into programs, highlighting missed opportunities for earlier cultural shifts.

recent_posts.title: Quick accessibility analysis of Norwegian party websites just before election – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: An accessibility audit of 29 Norwegian political party websites reveals critical issues across all sites. Common problems include missing skip-to-content links (16 out of 29), alternative text issues (25 out of 29), color contrast failures (24 out of 29), and semantic markup problems (18 out of 29). The analysis demonstrates that automatic testing tools only catch about 30% of accessibility issues, while manual testing reveals deeper problems affecting users with disabilities who rely on assistive technologies.

recent_posts.title: We need to talk about your accessibility statement – Bogdan on Digital Accessibility (A11y)
recent_posts.summary: Many organizations create accessibility statements primarily for compliance rather than user benefit, often claiming partial conformance without meaningful detail. The Norwegian approach requires detailed WCAG success criteria reporting, making organizations more aware of actual accessibility issues. Effective accessibility statements should be regularly updated, provide genuine user support, and reflect real accessibility processes rather than serving as mere compliance checkboxes.
